pages.text: NDT non linear acoustics, Acoustic Agree AB Technology Applications Articles About us Nonlinear acoustic NDT method detecting hidden and visible cracks and defects Nondestructive testing (NDT) using non linear acoustics. You can hear nonlinear acoustic effects by t apping a cracked crystal glass. A pure uncomplicated tone is heard in a fresh non broken glass and a cracked damaged glass gives a broken complicated tone clearly stating something is wrong. This distorted sound is the nonlinear acoustic effect caused by damages. A buried or surface breaking crack is detected by "provoking" the inspected item with our invented Non-linear Acoustic Waves (NAW® technology). Cracks and other defects will change our transmitted "sound pulses" in a nonlinear way making defects detectable with our inspection system. When analyzing the resulting sound response signature our inspection equipment will calculate a "Damagevalue", a numerical value of the defects severity, higher "Damagevalue" equals a larger crack. Any material able carrying sound waves can be inspected utilizing NAW®-inspection technology. As the sound pulses travels through the objects structure complex geometries are not an issue. A drilled hole will "guide" the transmitted sound pulses around the hole circumference. The behaviour of a crack is nonlinear while a hole without cracks is not. A crack will be visible to NAW-inspection but the hole will not show since a hole is not a defect. Non linear acoustics enables easy and fast inspection of details regardless complex geometries. Inspection for industrial use. NAW-inspection enables inspection of any solid material that carries sound pulses. Inspection of steel beams, casted stainless steel, plastic, cast iron, laser welds, but and joint welds, glass, laminated metals, laminated plastics like carbon reinforced plastics and even rubber are some examples of materials we currently inspect. Inspection time can be optimized down to just a few seconds for highly automated applications. The inspection method is operator independent as the "damagevalue" is calculated in the equipment. NEW Application example : NAW®-inspection of hydropower turbine blades. The forces and stress on a water power turbine is continuous and relentless, and when needed the most there is no room for stoppage. A waterpower turbine operates in tough conditions and measuring status of all components is a difficult task and Nonlinear acoustic inspection technology NAW® is one available inspection method that can help localizing damages and estimate lifecycle to verify power generation is up to task. READ MORE HERE : Article: NAW-inspection of highpressure tubeheatexchanger : "Crack Detection in large tube exchangers" Mixing wrong chemicals in a chemical factory may impose danger. A pressurized tube heat exchanger transferring heat from one chemical to another requires the tube heatexchanger to be perfectly tight during temperature stress to receive expected stabile results. Inspecting a tube heatexchanger with hundreds of welded tubes efficiently for cracks is achieved with Acoustic Agree AB patented NDT method NAW®-inspection. NAW®-inspection enables both detection of cracks not visible in cold state as locating and evaluating damages for repair. READ MORE HERE : Application example : Forged crankshaft, dragracing car . A Pro Mod dragracing car produces 3-5000hp to run a quarter mile in 5 seconds. A supercharged 526 cui (8.6 liters) hemi V8 running on methanol puts an enormous stress on the crankshaft transferring all the power from the pistons to the wheels. To handle cost and time in preparing for a 5 second race inspecting state of engine parts such as the crankshaft before a race is essential having the engine in a known good condition. One inspection method to check health of engine parts is NAW®-inspection (Non-linear Acoustic Waves) locating and estimating severity of buried cracks. READ MORE HERE : Application example : NAW-Inspection of railway Manganese crossing Railway crossings exposed to intense traffic needs to withstand wear and are manufactured in steel with high managanese content. The grain size in manganese steel makes conventional ultrasonic inspection difficult or even impossible. This work displays the success using NAW®-inspection detecting status and damages in manganese crossing .... READ MORE HERE : Application example : NAW-Inspection of Turbine blades Turbine blades are exposed to stresses such as vibrations, pressure variations, temperatures and more. Inspecting turbine blades is challenging and by utilizing NAW®-inspection we can detect damages. A damage starts as rifts in the materials grain structure .... pages.text: Acoustic Agree AB non linear acoustic technology Technology Applications Articles About us Non linear acoustic technology : Nondestructive test method (NDT) Non linear acoustics Nonlinear acoustic methods are a type of nondestructive testing (NDT) that uses the material's nonlinear response to sound waves to detect and characterize flaws like cracks, voids, and dislocations, which are often missed by conventional NDT methods.The non-destructive testing method is used for detecting, localizing and quantifying hidden and visible damages as cracks, rifts and voids. Any material capable of transfer sound energy as steel, aluminium, copper, cast iron, stainless steel, casted stainless steel, alloys and more can be inspected using non-linear acoustics. Nonlinear acoustics is the distorted sound effects caused by deviations and imperfections in a sound carrier. An example is the complicated multilayered tone arising in a cracked crystal glass when tapped, or the distorted sound in a cracked church bell. Nonlinear acoustic effects are audible to the human ear but Acoustic Agree AB have discovered, refined and industrialized technologies to measure how broken an object are. It is then displayed with a simple numerical value we define "Damagevalue ". When provoking the inspected object with sound energy introduced into an object via our transmitter and measuring the response with our sensors a numerical "Damagevalue" is calculated. The "Damagevalue" indicates how broken the object is with both severity of damage and amount of damage. A low Damagevalue indicates a healthy object with no severe damages, a high Damagevalue indicates the object is damaged, having less strength, robustness or solidity. The location of the damage can also be determined. When inspecting the complete object all damages as buried and surface breaking cracks, voids, rifts or pores are discovered. The NAW®-inspection method may imprudent be described as running Acoustic Emission, AE, inspection and Acoustic Resonance Technology, ART, simultaneously at same time, but not necessarily provoke inspected objects to its resonance frequency and "listening" for other sound effects than Acoustic Emission inspection. Complex geometries is not an issue for sound pulses as sound fills the complete volume of the inspected item. A drilled hole will "guide" the transmitted sound pulses around the hole circumference. The behavior of a crack is nonlinear while a carefully drilled hole without cracks is not. A crack will be visible to NAW®-inspection but the drilled hole will not since a well drilled hole is not a defect. If the hole had been drilled with a bad drill bit small defects and cracks would have appeared in the hole circumference making the damages in the drilled holes circumference detectable to NAW®-inspection. Nonlinear acoustics enables easy and fast inspection of details regardless complex geometries. Kinetic pulses Sound is physically "vibrations" or "vibration waves/pulses". When our transmitter is attached to an object for inspection kinetic energy/pulses is introduced in to the object, the detail is vibrated with our "sound signature". A good healthy object will carry the kinetic pulses we introduced through its grain structure swift and efficiently. A damaged object with damages as a crack, rift, gap or void inside will have to conduct the kinetic pulses through the damaged area changing our sound signature in a non linear manner that is detected with our sensors. Example: NAW inspection of laser weld joint quality in steel plates. NAW®-inspection technology "Hammering" a defect such as a crack in a material with our transmitted sound pulses the transmitted sound pulses start bouncing around in cracks, rifts and gaps causing a noise we detect and quantify with our equipment. Cracks and other defects will change the transmitted sound pulses in a nonlinear way making defects detectable. When analyzing the resulting sound signature our inspection equipment will analyze the level of imperfections in the inspected object calculating the Damagevalue for the inspected item. Depending on material properties different materials allow sound pulses to be transported different. Example: NAW inspection for damage assessment Manganese crossing for intense traffic railways NAW®-inspection equipment Acoustic Agree AB designs, develops and manufactures all equipment in house as no one else in the world do what we do. Main part of NAW®-inspection equipment is signal generation, transmitter, receiver, signal conditioning and signal analyzing. The equipment is powered via 230VAC/10A and can be used in tough industrial environments. We offer automated inline inspection units for 5-10 second component verification as well as mobile field inspection systems. Inspection for industrial use NAW®-inspection enables inspection of any solid material that carries sound pulses. Inspection of steel beams, casted stainless steel, plastic, cast iron, laser welds, but- and lap- weld joints, glass, laminated metals, laminated plastics like carbon reinforced plastics and even rubber are some examples of materials we currently inspect. Inspection time can be optimized down to just a few seconds for highly automated applications. The inspection method is operator independent as the "damagevalue" is calculated in the equipment. Example: Different semi automated NAW-inspection systems in component production Field inspection Acoustic Agree AB offers field inspection of large assemblies as water power turbines, shafts and generators, large size pressure vessels (12 meter high, 4 meter diameter), converter rings (10 meter diameter, 1 meter high in 100 millimeter steel), high pressure hydraulic press (5.000 ton press force), marine crank shafts, high pressure tube heat exchangers (8 meter long), autoclaves, reactor vessels and more. NAW®-inspection enables inspection of any solid material that carries sound pulses as steel beams, casted stainless steel, cast iron, laser welds, but, lap and joint welds, alloys, glass structures, composite beams and laminated metals, laminated plastics as carbon reinforced plastics and even rubber. Example: Field inspection of Marine engine crank shaft and field inspection of large pressure tank Example: Field inspection of Water power station components. NAW®-inspection Technology examples Any sound carrying material can be inspected using NAW®-inspection. We have succesfully examined applications in steel, casted steel, steel welds, stainless steel, casted stainless steel, manganese, titanium, ceramics, aluminium, copper, copper welds, metal alloys used in additive manufaturing and 3D printing, plastics as polyethylene, pex, nylon, rubber, composites, carbon fiber reinforced composites, steel reinforced composites, glass and more. As long as the material can carry sound we can inspect the materials deficiencies using NAW®-inspection method. NAW®-inspection method can complement or replace following NDT methods : - X-ray - Eddy current testing - Ultrasound - Radiography - Radiotomography - CT scanning - Acoustic emission testing - Acoustic resonance testing - Magnetic particle testing - Visual inspection as dye coloring - Phased array Technical papers, white papers Below is a link to one of our technical papers.
